notes: This contract pins the bounded embedded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Flush Queue Request/Grant implementation to the exact C++ RTIambassador and FederateAmbassador declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. It verifies the official signatures, declared exception set, adapter symbols, and real Catch2 selectors. A timestamped non-regional attribute-update companion now exercises the same public request/grant surfaces with object passels, actual-grant, and optimistic-floor assertions. Regional explicit-source and default-source interaction companions exercise the same request/grant path with overlap-qualified timestamped receive callbacks and preserved sent-region metadata before FQG, including the supplied-empty marker for the private default source. A default-source timestamped attribute-update companion exercises one ordinary/default-region passel through FQR, TARA, and NMRA with callback-before-grant ordering and the supplied-empty marker. A mixed-member regional companion exercises the same callback path for one FQR, one TARA, and one NMRA recipient sharing a source-region overlap. A separate HLA_EVOKED future-input interaction companion submits two TSO payloads after FQR acceptance but before callback dispatch and proves both receive callbacks precede FQG; these are in-process callback-frontier cases, not remote transport evidence. The source-backed report-file regression records the accepted supplied logical-time boundary before the later distinct actual/optimistic Flush Queue Grant. The same dispatcher now supports the separately traced timestamped-save seam: it drains current TSO payloads, directly initiates an eligible constrained save before FQG, and applies the private grant state immediately before Flush Queue Grant. A six-member scenario combines this strict-FQR path with TAR, NMR, TARA, and NMRA; paired process-local HLA_EVOKED/HLA_IMMEDIATE restore cases recreate the still-pending FQR and emit its fresh FQG only after Federation Restored. It is not catalog evidence, protected-review evidence, package support, or a conformance claim.
